text: On day i you receive 1+2+...+i gifts. Count gifts over the first n days, modulo 998244353.
constraints: n very large (loop is too slow)
idea: Total is n(n+1)(n+2)/6. Use Python big ints, or remove factors of 2 and 3 first in C++.
pitfalls: Do not loop to n. Only reduce mod after dividing.

text: Altitudes at consecutive integer seconds. Count triples (i, i+1, i+2) where slope of the first step exceeds slope of the second.
idea: Time gaps are 1, so compare consecutive differences: a[i+1]-a[i] > a[i+2]-a[i+1].
pitfalls: Check every triple, not every third index.

text: Stack n distinct rectangles with none overhanging the one below (axis-aligned, lattice points). Count the ways.
idea: Sort by area descending. Equal-area congruent rectangles contribute k!. Count placements of each on the next larger, rotating as needed. Double if the biggest is not a square.
pitfalls: Squares cannot rotate. Equal areas with different shapes means 0 ways.

text: Convex polygon. Fewest segments to draw with no zero-area regions and total length at least k/2.
idea: Longest segment is the diameter. With d diameters of length l, up to d segments give d*l; beyond that each extra gives just under l. Answer is ceil(k/2 / l), adjusting for the exact-integer case.
pitfalls: Use integer arithmetic. A diameter that is a polygon side is invalid.

text: Build an n by n binary grid where every down/right path from top-left to bottom-right passes through exactly one 1.
idea: Valid grids are exactly one antidiagonal all 1s with everything else 0, and the antidiagonal has at least two cells.
pitfalls: n = 1 has no valid grid under this rule.

text: Given integers in 1..40 grouped in buckets of 10, count buckets with at least one given integer.
idea: Insert (x-1)//10 into a set and print its size.

text: Maintain a map from integers to integers. Operations: set many keys to one value; ask how many keys currently have a given value.
constraints: large n and q, many tests
idea: Keep count[value] alongside the map. On each change, decrement the old value and increment the new one. Query is one lookup.
pitfalls: Do not build an n-entry dict per test. Store only changed keys and treat missing as the default value.

text: Hidden binary string of 100 pairs, each pair 01 or 10. Guess characters one at a time and learn the truth after each. Get at least 60% right.
idea: Guess the first of each pair at random, then guess the second correctly since it is the opposite. Expected 75% correct, failure probability negligible.
pitfalls: A deterministic strategy can be defeated by the interactor. Flush after every output.

text: Directed graph on 1..n. Fewest edges to add so the only topological order is 1,2,...,n, or report impossible.
idea: Any edge j to i with i<j makes it impossible. Otherwise the answer is the number of missing edges (i, i+1).
pitfalls: Use a set, not a list, for membership. Read all m edges before deciding.

text: Given n, print s followed by n+1 copies of h.
idea: print('s' + 'h' * (n + 1))
pitfalls: Off by one in the count.

text: Liked numbers have every digit exactly one more than the digit to its left. For up to 1e5 queries n (up to 1e8), find the smallest liked number at least n.
constraints: t up to 1e5, n up to 1e8
idea: Liked numbers are substrings of 123456789, only 45 of them. Sort and bisect. The answer always exists.
pitfalls: No leading zero, so the smallest digit is 1.

text: Choose real p_i summing to p to minimize the sum of p_i^2 / t_i.
idea: Optimal p_i is proportional to t_i, giving p^2 / sum(t).
pitfalls: Print with fixed decimals (for example :.9f).

text: Connected graph with n vertices and n edges, vertex values. Count simple paths whose endpoints differ in value by k.
idea: Find the single cycle, treat hanging trees. Same-tree pairs have one path, all other pairs have two. Answer = 2*(all qualifying pairs) - (qualifying pairs inside one tree).
pitfalls: Check ordered vs unordered pairs and whether k can be 0.

text: n <= 20 and you must choose a subset or ordering.
technique: bitmask DP or brute force over 2^n
idea: 2^n * n is fine up to about 20.
pitfalls: n <= 12 can allow n! permutations.

text: All-pairs shortest paths on a small graph.
idea: O(n^3) triple loop with the middle vertex outermost.
pitfalls: Loop order matters.

text: Find the smallest X such that a condition holds, and the condition gets easier as X grows.
idea: Write a feasibility check and bisect on X.
pitfalls: Make sure the check is truly monotone.

text: Shortest path in a graph with nonnegative edge weights.
idea: Pop smallest distance, skip stale entries, relax neighbors.
pitfalls: Negative edges need Bellman-Ford. Weights only 0/1 use 0-1 BFS.

text: Add edges one at a time and repeatedly ask whether two vertices are connected, or merge groups.
idea: Path compression plus union by size. A union that returns False means a cycle.

text: Order tasks given 'A must come before B' rules; detect impossibility.
idea: Kahn's algorithm. If not all vertices are output, there is a cycle.

text: Count the ways to reach a target using items, where order may or may not matter.
idea: dp[x] from smaller x. Loop items outside for combinations, outside the amount loop for orderings.
pitfalls: Loop order decides combinations vs permutations.

text: Longest increasing subsequence of an array.
idea: Maintain the smallest tail for each length, bisect to place each element. O(n log n).
pitfalls: bisect_left for strict, bisect_right for non-decreasing.

text: Select the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.
idea: Sort by end, take an interval if it starts after the last taken ends.
pitfalls: Sorting by start fails.

text: Process tasks with deadlines or merge items repeatedly choosing the cheapest.
idea: Keep a priority queue and always take the best candidate.
pitfalls: State why greedy is safe (exchange argument).

text: Count something modulo 998244353 involving choose or arrangements.
idea: Precompute fact and inverse fact, nCr = fact[n]*inv[r]*inv[n-r] mod p.
pitfalls: Use pow(x, p-2, p) for the inverse.

text: Many point updates and prefix or range sum queries.
idea: Both give O(log n) per operation.
pitfalls: Fenwick is 1-indexed.

text: For each element, find the next greater element to its right.
idea: Keep a stack of decreasing values and pop while the new value is larger.

text: Smallest convex polygon containing a point set, or farthest pair of points.
idea: Monotone chain hull, then calipers for the diameter.
pitfalls: Use integer cross products. Handle collinear points.

text: Find all occurrences of a pattern in a text in linear time.
idea: Prefix function on pattern + separator + text.
